proposed.text: BP 344 specifies warning tactile blocks before escalators and passenger conveyors. What are the required depth of the tactile strip and its setback distance from the landing plate or hazard edge?

options.text: 300 mm depth installed 300 mm before the hazard, spanning the full width of the escalator
300 mm depth installed 600 mm before the hazard, spanning the full width of the escalator
600 mm depth installed 300 mm before the hazard, centered on the escalator only
600 mm depth installed 300 mm before the hazard, spanning the full width of the escalator

rationale.summary: Escalator tactile: 600 mm depth, 300 mm setback from hazard, full-width coverage.
rationale.explanation: The mnemonic from the article is '600 deep, 300 back, full width.' The 600 mm depth gives a visually impaired user sufficient tactile surface to detect the warning before reaching the moving steps. The 300 mm setback keeps the strip clear of the metal landing plate. Full-width coverage prevents bypass. Option B inverts the two numbers — the most common exam trap.
common_misconceptions: Inverting the numbers: 300 mm depth and 600 mm setback instead of 600 mm depth and 300 mm setback
Thinking the strip only needs to cover the center lane rather than the full width

proposed.explanation: Escalator tactile rule: 600 mm depth, 300 mm setback, full width — never invert these two numbers.
